newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium stocks at one year low.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium stocks at one year low.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium stocks have become a focus of market attention, falling fallen by 14,275 tonnes over the past week to stand at a one year low of 778,350 tonnes.
Elsewhere, total copper stocks rose by 4,425 tonnes, while inventories of lead built by 2,350 tonnes.
Traders and analysts said the fall in aluminium stocks over the week reflected robust physical demand, which has resulted in sizeable drawdowns from the January 1997 peak of around 968,000 tonnes.
Physical demand in the U.S. is said to be strong, prompting further moves of aluminium from European warehouses.
"Overall demand is good and has the potential to grow near-term," one LME floor trader said.
Flemings Global Mining Group noted the fall in aluminium stocks has seen the stock/consumption ratio cascade to less than one week away from critical levels.
"We are keenly awaiting the Monday IPAI aluminium stock report," they said in a market report.
"The 110,000 tonne fall in February was stunning, a repeat would be dynamite," they added.
But some traders and analysts, while believing nearby demand was strong, were more cautious, suggesting that the movement of metal was into financing deals or to meet long term contracts.

Analyst Ted Arnold of Merrill Lynch said in a recent precious metals and base metal report the good part of the stock falls over the last two weeks have not gone into consumption and have only been taken off warrant and therefore not counted as LME registered material.

Arnold noted the practice of "white-lining" where stock can be taken off warrant but can actually be in the same warehouse complex and still owned by the same merchants, banks or investment funds who owned it before.
Chinese exports and slow physical demand saw lead stocks gain by 2,350 tonnes on the week to stand at 116,300 tonnes. But demand is expected to pickup as trade stocks in the U.S. are low.

Alloy stocks continued to fall against the backdrop of physical demand, a lack of scrap material and sound fundamentals. Stock continued to flow from the UK to the Far East. Once alloy stock is removed from LME warehouses it can not be put back on warrant.
Copper stocks gained by 4,425 tonnes to 153,350 tonnes and year to date stocks have risen by 23,575 tonnes.
But traders said end-user demand is moving in to a higher gear and one expected copper inventories to fall by around 10,000 tonnes in the next two weeks.
